# The harness beats the model

::: {.callout-note}
Draft brief, tier C: skeleton. Bullets and references compiled from source discussions 01–08 (2026-11-16). `[LAB n]`, `[RESEARCH]`, `[PLAN]` and `[VERIFY]` mark what is still open. `vault:` paths point into the Obsidian vault.
:::

**Outcome (draft, #2):** show that a harness change beats a model change for a given task, and pick the cheapest model that passes. Check: a naive vs an adjusted harness over the same cases; the report names the winner.

## Bullets available now
- Definition: "harness is the coding agent, agent loop or orchestrator (it's the wrapper around your workflow and prompts and tools)" (06).
- The yardstick: a harness "should MAXIMIZE agency, and MINIMIZE the cognitive load of the human. everything less than that shows the harness has room for improvement (and self-improvement!)" (01).
- Tests and measurements "must be a part of the harness" (01).
- Encode preferences so the model can't ignore them. This answers the vendor's advice to delete hooks that only encode preferences: "the trick with a good framework is to encode your preferences in a way the model can't ignore" (03).
- Answer, don't ignore, the vendor's counter-position: "With the actual code in front of it, Claude is usually better placed to make that call than a rule you wrote in advance" (03, source page). Shannon's setup has 26 hooks.
- Moving a rule from the prompt into the harness is a measured decision: "we should be able to correlate prompt changes into harness changes" (03).
- Vocabulary: the page's two-column table of what the model reads vs what the harness executes. It's a vendor framing with no data (03).
- An agent must not be able to write its own harness config. CVE-2026-25725 (Claude Code `settings.json` hooks), CVE-2026-26268 (Cursor git hooks), the IDEsaster series (07). `[VERIFY]` the CVE numbers at NVD.
- What I gave up: builders over-build controls, and the owner removes them. The content gate and the protected-path skip rule were both removed on 2026-11-12 (03, Claude).
